# ToolRank: full rankings

Last updated 2026-10-18. Source: https://toolrank.io/. Editorial ranking; position 1 = top pick. Pricing labels: free / freemium / paid (as listed; verify with vendor).


## AI Assistants

General-purpose AI chat assistants for everyday questions, writing and thinking.
Page: https://toolrank.io/best/ai-assistants/

1. ChatGPT (freemium; audience: both): Most versatile general assistant for drafting. https://chatgpt.com
2. Claude (freemium; audience: both): Strong long-form writing quality and natural tone. https://claude.ai
3. Google Gemini (freemium; audience: both): Google's assistant for drafting and editing, integrated with Workspace. https://gemini.google.com
4. Microsoft Copilot (freemium; audience: both): Microsoft's assistant, also built into Word and Outlook. https://copilot.microsoft.com
5. Grok (freemium; audience: consumer): xAI's assistant with real-time X data. https://grok.com
6. Le Chat (Mistral) (freemium; audience: both): Mistral AI's assistant with web search, documents and fast answers. https://chat.mistral.ai

## Coding & App Building

Build apps from a prompt, or code faster with AI pair programmers and agents.
Page: https://toolrank.io/best/coding/

1. Cursor (freemium; audience: business): AI-native code editor with strong agent mode and codebase context. https://www.cursor.com
2. Claude Code (paid; audience: business): Anthropic's terminal-based agentic coding tool. https://www.anthropic.com/claude-code
3. GitHub Copilot (freemium; audience: business): Most widely integrated assistant across IDEs and GitHub. https://github.com/features/copilot
4. Lovable (freemium; audience: consumer): Prompt-to-full-stack web app builder aimed at non-developers. https://lovable.dev
5. Bolt.new (freemium; audience: consumer): Builds and runs full-stack apps in the browser from a prompt. https://bolt.new
6. Windsurf (freemium; audience: business): Agentic IDE from Cognition, renamed Devin Desktop in June 2026. https://windsurf.com
7. OpenAI Codex (paid; audience: business): OpenAI's coding agent across CLI, IDE and cloud. https://openai.com/codex
8. v0 (freemium; audience: consumer): Vercel's generator for React/Next.js UIs and apps, deploys to Vercel. https://v0.app
9. Replit (freemium; audience: both): Replit Agent builds, hosts and deploys apps from one cloud workspace. https://replit.com
10. Cline (free; audience: business): Open-source autonomous coding agent for VS Code; bring your own model. https://cline.bot
11. Devin (paid; audience: business): Cognition's autonomous software engineering agent, now on the same plans as Devin Desktop. https://devin.ai
12. Kiro (freemium; audience: business): AWS's spec-driven agentic IDE and CLI, the successor to Amazon Q Developer. https://kiro.dev
13. Zed (freemium; audience: business): Fast open-source code editor with built-in AI agent and edit predictions. https://zed.dev
14. Amp (freemium; audience: business): Agentic coding tool for terminal and editors, spun out of Sourcegraph in 2025. https://ampcode.com
15. OpenHands (free; audience: business): Open-source, model-agnostic autonomous coding agent with a free cloud tier. https://www.openhands.dev
16. Aider (free; audience: business): Open-source terminal pair programmer that commits to git. https://aider.chat
17. JetBrains AI (Junie) (paid; audience: business): JetBrains' AI in IntelliJ-based IDEs; Junie is now part of JetBrains Air. https://junie.jetbrains.com/
18. Gemini CLI (free; audience: business): Google's open-source terminal coding agent powered by Gemini. https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli
19. Base44 (freemium; audience: both): Prompt-to-app builder with built-in database, auth and hosting; owned by Wix. https://base44.com
20. Google AI Studio (Build) (free; audience: both): Google's AI Studio builds and deploys Gemini-powered apps from a prompt. https://aistudio.google.com
21. Firebase Studio (free; audience: both): Google's cloud workspace for prototyping full-stack apps with Gemini. https://firebase.studio
22. Create.xyz (Anything) (freemium; audience: consumer): Prompt-to-app builder for web and mobile apps. https://www.createanything.com
23. Kilo Code (freemium; audience: business): Open-source coding agent for VS Code and JetBrains. https://kilo.ai
24. Rork (freemium; audience: consumer): Builds native mobile apps (React Native) from a prompt. https://rork.com
25. Softgen (paid; audience: consumer): AI web app builder producing Next.js apps with Firebase/Supabase. https://softgen.ai
26. Tempo (freemium; audience: consumer): Visual React editor with AI that generates and edits code. https://www.tempo.new
27. Same (freemium; audience: consumer): Clones or builds web apps from a prompt or URL. https://same.new
28. Macaly (freemium; audience: consumer): Prompt-to-website and app builder for non-developers. https://www.macaly.com
29. Figma Make (freemium; audience: both): Figma's prompt-to-app feature that turns designs and prompts into working prototypes. https://www.figma.com/make/
30. Augment Code (paid; audience: business): Coding agent built for large codebases with deep context. https://www.augmentcode.com
31. Bubble (freemium; audience: both): Established no-code platform with an AI app generator. https://bubble.io
32. Webflow (freemium; audience: both): Visual website builder with AI site and page generation. https://webflow.com
33. Factory (paid; audience: business): Droids: coding agents for terminal, IDE and CI. https://factory.com
34. Framer (freemium; audience: both): Design-first website builder with AI page generation. https://www.framer.com
35. Warp (freemium; audience: business): Agentic terminal and development environment. https://www.warp.dev
36. Dyad (freemium; audience: consumer): Free, local, open-source app builder; bring your own model keys. https://www.dyad.sh
37. OpenCode (free; audience: business): Open-source terminal coding agent supporting many models. https://opencode.ai
38. vibe-wise (free; audience: consumer): Claude Code/Codex plugin that teaches you to build while AI writes the code. New open-source launch on GitHub. https://github.com/nykooi1/vibe-wise
39. scroll-craft (free; audience: consumer): Agent skill for building premium scroll-driven websites. New open-source launch on GitHub. https://github.com/nateherkai/scroll-craft
40. CodeRabbit (paid; audience: business): AI code reviews on pull requests. https://www.coderabbit.ai
41. shadcn lint (free; audience: consumer): Agent-first linter for Tailwind design systems. New open-source launch on GitHub. https://github.com/shadcn-ui/lint
42. Qodo (paid; audience: business): AI code review and test generation. https://www.qodo.ai
43. Magpie (freemium; audience: business): Menu-bar app to run any coding agent (Codex, Claude Code) on any model. New open-source launch on GitHub. https://usemagpie.ai
44. Mono (monocode) (freemium; audience: business): A GUI for your coding agents. New open-source launch on GitHub. https://usemono.dev
45. OmniRush (freemium; audience: business): Desktop coding agent with free access to frontier models. New open-source launch on GitHub. https://omnirush.ai
46. jevgrep (free; audience: business): CLI for coding agents to find code by asking what it does. New open-source launch on GitHub. https://github.com/dzhng/jevgrep
47. coucou (freemium; audience: business): Tiny Mac-notch/iPhone companion that keeps an eye on your AI coding agents. New open-source launch on GitHub. https://louis-cfm.github.io/coucou/
48. Tabnine (paid; audience: business): Privacy-focused AI code assistant, acquired by Tricentis in 2026. https://www.tabnine.com
49. Cody (Sourcegraph) (paid; audience: business): Sourcegraph's AI coding assistant; Free and Pro discontinued in 2025, Enterprise only. https://sourcegraph.com/docs/cody
50. Amazon Q Developer (freemium; audience: business): AWS coding assistant, closed to new sign-ups since May 2026 and being replaced by Kiro. https://aws.amazon.com/q/developer/
51. Codeium (freemium; audience: business): Former name of Windsurf; codeium.com now redirects to Devin Desktop. https://codeium.com
52. Continue (free; audience: business): Open-source coding agent, acquired by Cursor in 2026; no longer maintained. https://www.continue.dev
53. Roo Code (free; audience: business): Open-source VS Code coding agent; shut down 15 May 2026. https://github.com/RooCodeInc/Roo-Code

9. Leonardo.Ai (freemium; audience: consumer): Image and video generation platform with fine-tuned models; owned by Canva. https://leonardo.ai
10. Stability AI (freemium; audience: both): Maker of Stable Diffusion open image models. https://stability.ai
11. Canva AI (freemium; audience: both): Canva's design platform with built-in AI image generation. https://www.canva.com

## Comparisons (facts checked 16 Oct 2026)

- Cursor vs Claude Code: https://toolrank.io/compare/cursor-vs-claude-code/ | Pick Cursor if you want an AI-first editor: a desktop app with agents, cloud automations and code review, and a free tier to try it. Pick Claude Code if you live in the terminal and want an agent that works across your repo. It has no free tier of its own and comes with a paid Claude plan (Pro from $17/month billed annually). Many developers use both: Cursor for editing, Claude Code for long agentic tasks.
- Cursor vs GitHub Copilot: https://toolrank.io/compare/cursor-vs-github-copilot/ | Pick GitHub Copilot if you want to keep your current editor. It plugs into VS Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains, Eclipse and Xcode, plus GitHub.com itself, and Pro is $10/month. Pick Cursor if you're happy to switch editors for an AI-native one, where agents, cloud automations and Bugbot review are part of the app rather than a plugin. Cursor's $8 Plus plan is cheaper on paper but limited to Grok models. To use third-party models you need Premium ($30), and that usage is billed at API prices on top.
- Cursor vs Windsurf: https://toolrank.io/compare/cursor-vs-windsurf/ | Important first: Windsurf is now Devin Desktop. Cognition renamed it on 2 Jun 2026, and windsurf.com/pricing now redirects to Devin's pricing. Pick Cursor if you want a polished single-editor experience with plans from $8/month. Pick Windsurf/Devin Desktop if you want one screen to run many agents, both Devin's and third-party ones like Codex and Claude Agent via ACP. Its free plan includes unlimited Tab completions, and Pro is $20/month. On both, heavy use of frontier models ends up billed at API prices, so compare your usage, not the sticker price.
- Claude Code vs GitHub Copilot: https://toolrank.io/compare/claude-code-vs-github-copilot/ | Pick GitHub Copilot if you want help inside the editor you already use, a real free plan, and agents and code review tied to GitHub pull requests. Pro is $10/month. Pick Claude Code if you want a terminal agent that reads and changes your whole repo in long, multi-step runs. It costs more to start, since it comes with Claude Pro ($17/month annual), but you also get the full Claude app. Copilot suits teams standardising on GitHub. Claude Code suits developers who delegate bigger tasks from the command line.
- Claude Code vs Windsurf: https://toolrank.io/compare/claude-code-vs-windsurf/ | Windsurf has been renamed Devin Desktop (June 2026), so this is really Claude Code against Cognition's agent IDE. Pick Claude Code if you want Anthropic's agent in your terminal, bundled with a Claude subscription. Pick Windsurf/Devin Desktop if you want a graphical IDE with a free plan that can also host Claude Agent itself through ACP, next to Devin and Codex, in one Kanban view. Using Claude Agent inside Devin Desktop doesn't make the costs go away: model usage still comes from somewhere.
- Windsurf vs GitHub Copilot: https://toolrank.io/compare/windsurf-vs-github-copilot/ | Pick GitHub Copilot if you want to stay in VS Code, JetBrains, Visual Studio or Xcode and keep everything on GitHub. It's $10/month for Pro and runs in more editors than anything else here. Pick Windsurf, now Devin Desktop, if you'll switch to a dedicated agent IDE in exchange for running multiple local and cloud agents (Devin Cloud on Pro, $20/month) from one board. For teams, Copilot's seat model is simpler. Devin Desktop Teams has an $80/month minimum plus $40 per full seat.
- Cursor vs Continue.dev: https://toolrank.io/compare/cursor-vs-continue-dev/ | This matchup has a twist: Cursor acquired Continue in 2026. Continue's GitHub repo is now read-only and 2.0.0 was its final release. Pick Cursor if you want a maintained product with ongoing updates. Continue's open-source extension still runs with your own model keys or local models, so it's only worth considering if you need a frozen, self-run setup and accept that nothing will be fixed. If you liked Continue's bring-your-own-model approach, Cline is the closest maintained alternative on ToolRank.
- Cursor vs Cody (Sourcegraph): https://toolrank.io/compare/cursor-vs-cody/ | For individuals this isn't a real choice any more. Sourcegraph stopped new Cody Free and Pro sign-ups in June 2025 and discontinued those plans, and its successor product Amp spun out as a separate company in December 2025. Pick Cursor if you're an individual or small team. Pick Cody only if your company already runs Sourcegraph Enterprise (from a $16K annual minimum) and wants AI grounded in Sourcegraph's code search across very large codebases.
- Claude Code vs Aider: https://toolrank.io/compare/claude-code-vs-aider/ | Both live in the terminal, so the difference is the business model. Aider is free and open source (Apache-2.0). You plug in any model, including DeepSeek or a local one, and pay only your provider. Every change is a git commit you can undo. Claude Code is Anthropic's own agent, bundled into Claude plans from $17/month, built for longer autonomous runs across a repo. Pick Aider for cost control and model freedom. Pick Claude Code if you already pay for Claude and want the most capable agent from that vendor without wiring up API keys.
- Cursor vs Replit Agent: https://toolrank.io/compare/cursor-vs-replit-agent/ | These solve different problems. Replit Agent lives in the browser: describe an app and it builds, adds a database and deploys it, with no local setup. Core is $20/month ($18 annual) and includes $20 of model credit. Cursor is a desktop editor for working in your own repo, with agents, code review and plans from $8/month. Founders and non-specialists shipping a hosted app should start with Replit. Developers maintaining real codebases with their own tooling should pick Cursor.
- Claude Code vs Devin: https://toolrank.io/compare/claude-code-vs-devin/ | Pick Claude Code if you want to stay in the loop: it runs in your terminal on your machine, you watch it work, and you steer it. Pick Devin if you want to hand off tickets entirely. It runs in the cloud, takes tasks from Slack, Linear or Jira, and comes back with PRs on GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket. Devin's self-serve plans now start free, but cloud agents need Pro ($20/month). Claude Code starts at $17/month (annual) through Claude Pro.
- Cursor vs Bolt.new: https://toolrank.io/compare/cursor-vs-bolt-new/ | Pick Bolt.new if you want an app running in your browser in minutes from a prompt, with no install and no repo. Its free plan gives 300K tokens a day (1M a month) and Pro is $25/month. Pick Cursor if you're a developer working on an existing codebase, or you want full control over files, git and deployment. A common path is to prototype in Bolt, then move the code into Cursor once it needs real engineering.
- Cursor vs Lovable: https://toolrank.io/compare/cursor-vs-lovable/ | Pick Lovable if you're a founder, designer or non-developer who wants to chat an app into existence and host it on Lovable Cloud. The free plan gives 5 build credits a day, capped at 30 a month. Pick Cursor if you write code and want an AI editor and agents working in your own repo. Lovable's paid prices didn't render in the page text we fetched, so check its pricing page directly. Cursor's start at $8/month.
- Windsurf vs Continue.dev: https://toolrank.io/compare/windsurf-vs-continue-dev/ | Neither product exists under its old name. Windsurf is now Devin Desktop (Cognition, June 2026), and Continue was acquired by Cursor, with its repo read-only after a final 2.0.0 release. If you want something maintained, the real choice is Devin Desktop (free plan, Pro $20/month) or another live tool. Keep running Continue's open-source extension only if you need a self-run, bring-your-own-model setup and can live without updates.
- GitHub Copilot vs Continue.dev: https://toolrank.io/compare/github-copilot-vs-continue-dev/ | Continue was long the open-source answer to Copilot, but Continue has been acquired by Cursor and is no longer maintained. Pick GitHub Copilot if you want a supported assistant in VS Code, JetBrains and more, with a free plan and Pro at $10/month. Only stay on Continue's final open-source release if you specifically need local models or full control and accept frozen software. If open source matters to you, compare Copilot with Cline instead.
- Cursor vs Zed AI: https://toolrank.io/compare/cursor-vs-zed-ai/ | Pick Zed if speed comes first: it's a fast native open-source editor that stays free forever when you bring your own API keys or external agents like Claude Agent and Codex CLI. Pro is $10/month with unlimited edit predictions and $5 of tokens. Pick Cursor if you want the deepest built-in agent features, like cloud agents, automations and Bugbot code review, and don't mind a VS Code-style editor. Zed bills hosted usage at API list price plus 10%. Cursor bills third-party models at API list price on Premium.
- Claude Code vs Amazon Q Developer: https://toolrank.io/compare/claude-code-vs-amazon-q-developer/ | Amazon Q Developer is being retired. AWS closed new sign-ups on 15 May 2026, the Q CLI became Kiro CLI, and IDE plugins and paid subscriptions reach end of support on 30 Apr 2027. New users can't choose it. Pick Claude Code for a terminal agent from Anthropic, from $17/month. If you're tied to AWS, compare Claude Code with Kiro, AWS's successor, which also offers Claude models and has a free tier.
- Cursor vs Tabnine: https://toolrank.io/compare/cursor-vs-tabnine/ | Pick Cursor if you're an individual or a team wanting a self-serve AI editor today, with a free plan and paid plans from $8/month. Tabnine was acquired by Tricentis in 2026, and tabnine.com now redirects to Tricentis, so we couldn't re-verify its current plans. Its historical strength is private, on-prem and air-gapped deployment for enterprises. If that's your requirement, contact Tricentis directly. Otherwise Cursor is the straightforward choice.
- Claude Code vs Codeium: https://toolrank.io/compare/claude-code-vs-codeium/ | Codeium no longer exists as a brand. It became Windsurf, and Windsurf became Devin Desktop in June 2026. codeium.com now redirects to Devin Desktop. So the real comparison is Claude Code against Devin Desktop. Pick Claude Code for Anthropic's terminal agent with a Claude plan (from $17/month). Pick Devin Desktop if you want a free IDE with unlimited Tab completions and an agent board, with Pro at $20/month.
- Windsurf vs Cody (Sourcegraph): https://toolrank.io/compare/windsurf-vs-cody/ | Both have changed a lot. Windsurf is now Devin Desktop, and Cody is enterprise-only after Sourcegraph discontinued Free and Pro in 2025. For an individual or small team, Devin Desktop is the only one of the two you can sign up for: Free, or Pro at $20/month. Cody makes sense only inside an existing Sourcegraph Enterprise deployment (from $16K/year), where its value is code-search context across huge monorepos.
- Cursor vs Roo Code: https://toolrank.io/compare/cursor-vs-roo-code/ | Roo Code shut down on 15 May 2026 and its GitHub repo is archived, so pick Cursor if you want a maintained AI editor. If you used Roo for its open-source, bring-your-own-model agent in VS Code, the Roo team itself points to Cline (the project Roo was forked from) or the community fork ZooCode. Kilo Code is another Roo-lineage option listed on ToolRank.
- Claude Code vs Cline: https://toolrank.io/compare/claude-code-vs-cline/ | Pick Cline if you want the agent free and open source, inside VS Code (or the CLI), with any model from Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, OpenRouter, Bedrock and more. You pay only for inference, at cost or with your own keys. Pick Claude Code if you'd rather pay one Claude subscription (from $17/month) than per-token bills, and you're happy in the terminal. Heavy users often find a subscription more predictable than paying per token. Light users usually spend less with Cline.
- Cursor vs OpenHands: https://toolrank.io/compare/cursor-vs-openhands/ | Pick OpenHands if you want an autonomous agent you can run locally for free, self-host, or audit line by line. It's MIT-licensed and model-agnostic, with a free cloud tier capped at 10 conversations a day. Pick Cursor if you want an editor first, where you code alongside agents with completions, review and cloud agents in one polished app. Teams with strict data rules lean towards OpenHands' self-hosting. Individual developers usually get more done day to day in Cursor.
- GitHub Copilot vs Amazon Q Developer: https://toolrank.io/compare/github-copilot-vs-amazon-q-developer/ | New users can only pick one of these: AWS stopped new Amazon Q Developer sign-ups on 15 May 2026, and plugins and paid subscriptions end on 30 Apr 2027. Pick GitHub Copilot for a supported assistant across VS Code, JetBrains, Visual Studio, Eclipse and Xcode, with a free plan and Pro at $10/month. Existing Q customers with Java or .NET upgrades in flight should finish them before the cutoff and plan a move. AWS's own path is Kiro.
- Cursor vs JetBrains AI Assistant: https://toolrank.io/compare/cursor-vs-jetbrains-ai-assistant/ | Pick JetBrains AI if IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm or another JetBrains IDE is home. AI Pro is $10/month on personal pricing, and JetBrains Air now runs Junie alongside Claude Agent, Codex and Copilot, with your own keys if you like. Pick Cursor if you're on VS Code or don't mind switching, and want an editor built around AI from the ground up. The deciding factor is usually your IDE: JetBrains users rarely want to give up its refactoring and inspections.

## Best-of guides (facts last checked 18 Oct 2026)

- Best AI coding tools for $20 a month or less: https://toolrank.io/best-of/ai-coding-tools-under-20-a-month/ | If you want the most capable tool for $20 a month or less, start with Cursor. Its Plus plan is $8/month, but it only includes Grok models. Claude Code comes with Claude Pro, at $17/month billed annually or $20 billed monthly. GitHub Copilot Pro ($10/month) is the pick if you want to stay in your current IDE. Zed Pro and JetBrains AI Pro are also $10/month. Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf), Devin, Kiro, Amp and Replit Core all list a $20 plan. Every price below is from the vendor's own pricing page, checked 16 Oct 2026.
- Best AI coding tools under $50 a month: https://toolrank.io/best-of/ai-coding-tools-under-50-a-month/ | Under $50 a month, Cursor Premium ($30/month) is our top pick. It gets 4x Plus usage, cloud agents, Bugbot reviews and third-party models, though those models are billed at API list price. Claude Code through Claude Pro ($20 monthly) is the terminal pick. Claude Max starts at $100, which is over this cap. GitHub Copilot Pro+ is $39/month, Kiro Pro+ $40/user/month, JetBrains AI Ultimate $30/month and Bolt Pro $25/month. All prices were checked on vendor pages on 16 Oct 2026.
- Best free AI coding tools (no subscription): https://toolrank.io/best-of/free-ai-coding-tools/ | For AI coding with no subscription, Cline is our top pick. It's an open-source agent for VS Code and the CLI, and you pay only for model usage, with your own keys or at cost. Zed is free forever with your own API keys or external agents. Amp's Hobby plan is free with all features and bring-your-own keys. OpenHands is free to run locally, and its cloud tier allows 10 conversations a day. Aider is free, open-source terminal software. The catch: unless you run a local model, you still pay a model provider. If you want usage included at $0, see the free-tier list.
- Best AI coding tools for solo developers: https://toolrank.io/best-of/ai-coding-tools-for-solo-developers/ | For solo developers, Cursor is our top pick. It's a complete AI editor with a free tier, and Plus is $8/month. Claude Code (from $17/month annually via Claude Pro) suits terminal-first developers. GitHub Copilot is free to start, Pro is $10, and it works in most IDEs. On a tight budget, Zed, Cline and Aider cost nothing to use with your own model keys. Every price is from the vendor's individual plans, checked 16 Oct 2026.
- Best AI coding tools for small teams: https://toolrank.io/best-of/ai-coding-tools-for-small-teams/ | For small teams, Cursor Teams ($30+/user/month, pooled usage) is our top pick. GitHub Copilot is the easiest pick if your team is on GitHub, but we haven't verified its business pricing yet. Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf) Teams costs an $80/month minimum plus $40 per full seat, for up to 200 users. Zed Business is $30/seat. Amp Teams adds shared billing and SSO at no extra charge. Bolt Teams is $30/member. Claude's Team premium seat, which includes Claude Code, is $100/seat/month billed annually. Prices were checked on vendor pages on 16 Oct 2026.
- Best AI coding agents in 2026: https://toolrank.io/best-of/ai-coding-agents/ | For an agent that works across your repo, Claude Code is our top pick: Anthropic's terminal agent, included with Claude Pro ($17/month annually). Cursor pairs its editor with agents and cloud automations. Devin takes whole tickets in the cloud and opens pull requests, but cloud agents need Pro ($20/month). Cline and OpenHands are open-source agents where you pay only for inference. Amp lets you reuse existing model subscriptions. Kiro is AWS's spec-driven agent with a perpetual free tier. Checked 16 Oct 2026.
- Best AI pair programmers: https://toolrank.io/best-of/ai-pair-programmers/ | For an AI that works alongside you rather than taking whole tasks, GitHub Copilot is our top pick. It works as a pair programmer inside your IDE and GitHub, it runs in VS Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains, Eclipse and Xcode, it has a free plan, and Pro is $10/month. Cursor is the AI-native editor option, with a free tier and Plus at $8/month. Zed offers edit predictions in a fast editor, free with your own keys or $10 for Pro. JetBrains AI Pro is $10/month for JetBrains users. Aider is a free, open-source pair programmer for the terminal. Checked 16 Oct 2026.
- Best AI coding tools for beginners: https://toolrank.io/best-of/ai-coding-tools-for-beginners/ | If you're new to code and want to build something, start with Lovable or Bolt.new. Both turn plain-language prompts into web apps in the browser and have free plans. Lovable gives 5 build credits a day, up to 30 a month. Bolt gives 300K tokens a day and 1M a month. Replit builds, hosts and deploys from one browser workspace, with Core at $20/month. If you want to learn to code in a real editor, GitHub Copilot Free and Cursor Free cost nothing to start. Checked 16 Oct 2026.
- Best AI tools for building full-stack apps: https://toolrank.io/best-of/ai-tools-for-building-full-stack-apps/ | To go from a prompt to a running full-stack app, Bolt.new is our top pick. It builds, runs and deploys in the browser, has a generous token-based free tier, and Pro is $25/month. Lovable turns chat into web apps with hosting on Lovable Cloud, but we couldn't verify its paid prices. Replit covers prompt, build, database and deploy in one workspace, from $20/month. v0 generates React/Next.js apps that deploy to Vercel. Cursor fits developers who want full control in their own repo. Checked 16 Oct 2026.
- Best AI coding tools with a free tier: https://toolrank.io/best-of/ai-coding-tools-with-free-tier/ | For a free plan that includes AI usage with no API key, Cursor Free is our top pick, with limited agent and chat requests. GitHub Copilot Free has limited chat and agent usage but no code review or cloud agent. Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf) Free has a light agent quota and unlimited Tab completions. Kiro gives a perpetual 50 credits. Bolt gives 300K tokens a day. Lovable gives 5 build credits a day. Devin Free has a light quota without cloud agents. All limits were checked on vendor pages on 16 Oct 2026.

## New this week (as of 2026-10-16)

- 2026-10-15 Muse Spark Open (model): Meta releases the weights for Muse Spark Open, a natively multimodal 816B-parameter (42B active) model with a 1M-token context, built for coding and agentic work. Runs on two M5 Ultra Mac Studios via MLX; Muse Model License. https://research.meta.ai/blog/muse-spark-open
- 2026-10-15 NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL (model): NVIDIA's open 120B-parameter multimodal model for always-on agents, available now on Hugging Face, OpenRouter, ModelScope and as NVIDIA NIM. Released alongside Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B for local 24GB systems. https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/nemotron-3-5-super-vl/
- 2026-10-15 FLUX 3 Image Klein (model): Black Forest Labs' 5.6B open-weights model for text-to-image, editing and multi-reference generation (up to 10 images), with native 4K and bounding-box control. Runs on 8GB-VRAM GPUs with the INT8 build; also in the BFL API. https://bfl.ai/blog/flux-3-image-klein
- 2026-10-15 Mistral Timestral (model): Mistral's first family of time-series foundation models (5M to 209M parameters) for probabilistic, multivariate forecasting. Runs on CPU; Modified MIT licence. https://mistral.ai/news/timestral/
- 2026-10-15 Claude Code Review (GA) (launch): Anthropic's Code Review is out of research preview for Claude Team and Enterprise. Reviews run automatically on new PRs, now about 3x faster, with Quick, Standard or Deep levels per repository. https://claude.com/resources/articles/code-review-is-now-generally-available
- 2026-10-15 morluto/rea (github): GitHub weekly trending: reverse-engineer apps down to native binaries with agents. https://github.com/morluto/rea
- 2026-10-15 heygen-com/hyperframes (github): GitHub weekly trending: write HTML, render video, built for agents. https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes
- 2026-10-15 thedotmack/claude-mem (github): GitHub weekly trending: persistent cross-session memory for coding agents. https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem
- 2026-10-15 earthtojake/text-to-cad (github): GitHub weekly trending: gives agents CAD capabilities. https://github.com/earthtojake/text-to-cad
- 2026-10-14 Grok Voice 3.0 (model): xAI's new speech-to-speech model, with sub-second latency, available today in the Voice Agent API at $0.08/min, the same price as Grok Voice 2.0. https://x.ai/news/grok-voice-3
- 2026-10-13 Liquid AI LFM2.5-24B-A2B (model): Open-weight 24B reasoning model with just 2B active parameters, built for fast, private agents on-device. 131K context; on Hugging Face and Liquid's Playground. https://www.liquid.ai/blog/lfm2-5-24b-a2b
